name: How do you know if pool resurfacing is enough or if the pool needs a full replaster and chip-out?

mainEntity.name: When can a pool be resurfaced over the existing surface, and when does the old finish need to be completely removed?
mainEntity.text: When can a pool be resurfaced over the existing surface, and when does the old finish need to be completely removed?

acceptedAnswer.text: The decision comes down to bond quality and the condition of the existing surface. If the finish is mostly intact and only shows normal wear, a new top layer may be possible. If there are hollow sounds when tapped, delamination, major spider cracking, recurring blistering, or several failed repairs, a full chip-out is usually safer because it removes weak material and gives the new finish a stable base. This matters in older pools common across Los Angeles neighborhoods where past repairs may have been done over damaged plaster. A contractor should inspect for soundness, shell movement, and moisture issues before recommending a method. The cheapest option is not always the best if it risks another failure within a few years. Homeowners should ask whether the estimate includes bond testing, surface prep, and removal of loose material, because those steps affect how long the new finish lasts.
acceptedAnswer.description: A simple resurface may work if the old finish is sound, well bonded, and only worn at the surface. A full chip-out is usually needed when there are hollow spots, widespread delamination, severe cracking, persistent staining, or multiple past overlays. The old surface condition determines whether new material will bond properly.
